'''Christoph Steinbeck''' (born 1966 in [[Neuwied]]<ref>{{Cite web | title=Archived copy | url=https://jungforscher-thueringen.de/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/20190620_22_SchuleMITWissenschaftThüringen.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211219215247/https://jungforscher-thueringen.de/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/20190620_22_SchuleMITWissenschaftTh%C3%BCringen.pdf | access-date=2024-12-15 | archive-date=2021-12-19}}</ref>) is a German chemist and has a professorship for [[analytical chemistry]], [[cheminformatics]] and [[chemometrics]] at the [[Friedrich Schiller Universität Jena|Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena]] in [[Thuringia]].<ref>{{Cite Q|Q34313323}}</ref><ref>{{Cite Q|Q34212022}}</ref>

==Education==
Steinbeck received his [[PhD]] from the [[University of Bonn]]<ref name="steinbeckphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Christoph|last=Steinbeck |title=LUCY, ein Programm zur Konstitutionsbestimmung aus Korrelations-NMR-Experimenten sowie Beispiele zur Identifizierung von Naturstoffen durch NMR-Spektroskopie |publisher=University of Bonn |date=1995 |author-link=Christoph Steinbeck |id={{DNB-IDN|948048905}}}}</ref> in 1995 for work on LUCY, a software program for [[structural elucidation]] from [[Nuclear magnetic resonance|nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)]] correlation experiments.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q50368945}}</ref> In 2003 he received his [[habilitation]].<ref name="habilitation">{{cite thesis |degree=Habilitation |first=Christoph|last=Steinbeck |title=Zur automatischen Strukturaufklärung organischer Verbindungen |publisher=University of Bonn |date=2003 |author-link=Christoph Steinbeck |id={{DNB-IDN|970193602}}}}</ref>

==Research==
Steinbeck's research interests<ref name="GS">{{Google Scholar id |name=Christoph Steinbeck}}</ref><ref name="DBLP">{{DBLP |name=Christoph Steinbeck}}</ref><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus}}</ref> have involved the elucidation of chemical structures of [[metabolite]]s. He was one of the first chemists to develop [[Open-source software|open source]] tools for cheminformatics. He initiated [[JChemPaint]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Krause | first1 = S. | last2 = Willighagen | first2 = E. | last3 = Steinbeck | first3 = C. | author-link3 = Christoph Steinbeck| title = JChemPaint – Using the Collaborative Forces of the Internet to Develop a Free Editor for 2D Chemical Structures | doi = 10.3390/50100093 | journal = Molecules | volume = 5 | issue = 12 | pages = 93–98 | year = 2000 | doi-access = free | hdl = 11858/00-001M-0000-0012-A15A-4 | hdl-access = free }}</ref> was founder of the [[Chemistry Development Kit]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Steinbeck | first1 = C.| author-link1 = Christoph Steinbeck | last2 = Han | first2 = Y. | last3 = Kuhn | first3 = S. | last4 = Horlacher | first4 = O. | last5 = Luttmann | first5 = E. | last6 = Willighagen | first6 = E. | doi = 10.1021/ci025584y | title = The Chemistry Development Kit (CDK): An Open-Source Java Library for Chemo- and Bioinformatics | journal = Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling | volume = 43 | issue = 2 | pages = 493–500 | year = 2003 | pmid =  12653513| pmc = 4901983}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Steinbeck | first1 = C. | author-link1 = Christoph Steinbeck| last2 = Hoppe | first2 = C. | last3 = Kuhn | first3 = S. | last4 = Floris | first4 = M. | last5 = Guha | first5 = R. | last6 = Willighagen | first6 = E. | doi = 10.2174/138161206777585274 | title = Recent Developments of the Chemistry Development Kit (CDK) - an Open-Source Java Library for Chemo- and Bioinformatics | journal = Current Pharmaceutical Design | volume = 12 | issue = 17 | pages = 2111–2120 | year = 2006 | pmid =  16796559| hdl = 2066/35445 | url = https://repository.ubn.ru.nl/bitstream/handle/2066/35445/35445_aut.pdf?sequence=3 | hdl-access = free }}</ref> and is responsible for leading the team working on [[ChEBI|Chemical Entities of Biological Interest (ChEBI)]].<ref>{{Cite journal

He became a professor for analytical chemistry, cheminformatics and chemometrics at the Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena in Thuringia, Germany in March 2017. Since 2020, Steinbeck is leading the German National Research Data Infrastructure for Chemistry (NFDI4Chem)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our Consortium |url=https://www.nfdi4chem.de/index.php/konsortium/ |access-date=6 March 2023 |website=NFDI4Chem |language=en-GB}}</ref> and in August 2022, he became vice President for digitalisation of the Friedrich Schiller University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The University of Jena establishes a new Vice President for Digitalisation |url=https://www.uni-jena.de/en/220719-vpdigitalisierung |access-date=6 March 2023 |website=Friedrich Schiller University Jena |date=19 July 2022 |language=en}}</ref> Together with a few other chemists he was a founder member of the [[Blue Obelisk]]<ref>{{Cite journal

Steinbeck was past [[editor-in-chief]] of the ''[[Journal of Cheminformatics]]'', past director of the [[Metabolomics]] Society,<ref>[http://www.metabolomicssociety.org/board_of_directors ''Metabolomics Society Board''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140323164342/http://www.metabolomicssociety.org/board_of_directors |date=23 March 2014 }}, website of Metabolomics Society</ref> past chair of the Computers-Information-Chemistry division of the [[German Chemical Society]], past trustee of the [[Chemical Structure Association]] Trust,<ref>Chemical Structure Association Newsletter, 2006, 12, http://www.csa-trust.org/news06/Issue12.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160326104624/http://www.csa-trust.org/news06/issue12.pdf/ |date=26 March 2016 }}</ref> and a lifetime member of the [[World Association of Theoretically Oriented Chemists]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.watoc.net/watoc.members.html|title=WATOC – Home|website=www.watoc.net|accessdate=19 December 2021}}</ref>
